column1: Despite the damp air, none of the books show signs of degradation.
Flasks and instruments, strewn about the chamber.
The stone slabs are designed to slide along the iron beams. Interesting.
Ouch. That hurt.
This stone slab has been refitted into a desk. Inventive.
Watch it!
You could drink out of the bottles. You should not.
Voices upstairs. And the smell of salt.
Piles of empty containers. You could move them with ease. Maybe.
Divine protection under a stern gaze.
You kick the bottom of a crate. Your foot hurts.
Jor left his mark across the bands. Today it is a universal sign of magic.
I'm sure this was a fun person once.
This guy... he just won't move!
Imported goods. The reciever is marked as 'HWBT'.
You need to pray.
This one's labeled, 'MISC'.
A place where DEATH ends.
A sealed vase. It's marked as 'organ disposal'.
A glow-glass. Very common magic item.
A great mountain of apples.
The air is cool in here. An esoteric effect.
The River calls to y o u.
Cleric speak to master. Now!
The Red Eye of Urth.
Nothing of interest back here.
Nature seeps through the cracks.
Old symbol of an old regime.
The tall dwarven walls of Tolstad. An amazing feat of engineering.
Servants. You hear them talking about how much of a dick Darrow is.
The goblin grins at you.
Welcome to the garden...
A broken statue of a cat. Cute.
The roots go deeper than you can imagine...
Bikes are cool. You should ride your bike more.
The Lady's apartments. Her favorites get to live above ground.
These stones are older than your soul.
The Goblin Garden is ahead. You feel it.
These walls are sturdy dwarven architecture. Modern. Late war period.
They are struggling after a terrible decision. How relatable.
The sacred river fights against red rocks.
You can see the apartment from here, across the river.
This is surely illegal.
A corner of Norvik, still standing in the Gate Era.
This takes gut.
<i>O, those poor few dreams wrought in zeal and doubt...<i>
What would happen if you jumped?
The Great Perch of Norvik.
A theatre fit for someone like you: a performer.
Grab the Hammer! For a GREEN COAST! <shake>AZGALISM FOREVER</shake>!
It's a long drop.
By Urth, how did they get this wagon down the stairs?
Such a sneaky staircase. Nice find.
You're going to retch.
A musky smell eminates from this passage. Fungal?
These railings follow the Safety Council's Standards of '22.
There are no funds, nor focus, needed to restore these structures.
You should apologize for this.
There is an esoteric effect in place here, stopping rainwater.
This walkway does not follow the Safety Council's Standards of '22.
The Halfway Bridge. It connects with The Palace, and the rest of southern Norvik.
Enclosed by the by, she keeps me back down...
The Dwarf and Urthfolk - together.
No! No way. Not a chance, dad!
Nope. Can't help from this side.
The name of the Tea Shop is illegible.
This road leads into central Tolstad. You have no business there.
The orc observes you with great interest.
This is beneath you. Get back on track.
Enjoy yourself, Romulus! You'll get scraps later...!
The ridge is slippery. Careful!
Chatter inside. An argument?
The mansion continues far and wide.
The boss.
A cozy nook.
All you need. This... is all you need.
There is some type of god in the machine, surely.
It reeks.
How the hell is this place still standing?
Laughter and debate once filled these seats.
It says, Joanna, CEO. Maior quam ullus rex.
Tripple D. The man, the myth, the lad-who-is-mad.
That son of a bitch. He's got a whole HOARD back here!
The Drakeslayer! Such an artwork.
It collapsed decades ago.
Looks like a Vourgeni air-binder. Probably counterfeit.
Hold on... is this tunnel connected to the TEA SHOP?
A not-so tiny dictator.
'All who pass, are mine to keep.'

Window to Waterlane.
You won't find your god here.
He looks upon you.
A grand entrance - or exit.
A speaker. They must have lines running through the walls.
Visken's lichhouse must be located within these walls. Just a bit further up.
The dragon herself.
The goblins chuckle as you walk past.
The throne of a modern dragon.
Something foul is fermenting here.
Several potion-boxes are marked with a tiny bird-symbol.
The DEPTHS. Of TOLSTAD.
The depths call to you.
The machine groans.
Unity of all folk.
Ah... Bagatelle! The goblin has some good taste then.
The goblin's neatness feels almost divine.
You don't really fit back there.
You do not need to relieve yourself.
He sure is the type to have a photo of himself on the wall.
Children's drawings on the wall.
A scholarly commendation of the Fordnip Commonwealth.
This rug is a fake Frukk Framm. How very glib.
Looks like an archive.
A framed article titled, 'Octavio Durelius, Hero of Waterlane!'
Spices and extracted juices of the most exotic varieties.
Moldy old wood. It gets real damn down here.
The never-sleeping docks of Waterlane- right below here.
These windows... the Freestriders have converted this building into a warehouse.
One of many Freestrider compounds in the city.
Deep. Groaning. The Bell of Waterlane.
No one can dismiss the dwarves' architectural genius.
A BELL of the CITY.
TORNA. The first of the river guilds.
You are WITHIN the red rock of Tolstad.
These pipes connect with the vast sewer system of Tolstad.
Excluding the anti-magic messaging, Freestriderism comes with great branding.
Stairs down to the bustling docks.

An altar to a heretical faith. Consecrate it!
Beware, the CRUNCH.
This is an awfully ominous hallway.
Please don't step on the literal human skulls.
You can see the whole survey from here.
A monster manual! But most pages are ruined.
These are the sewers below Waterlane.
You can hear the wind outside. An illusion, surely.
This vast array of knowledge...
The abyss will swallow your soul.
A red dragon, fallen to humanities greatness.
The dungeon continues far into the west-part of Tolstad.
The goblins are reclaiming the tunnel east. It's gotten real hot down there.
As the giant sky fell down...
He was here.
You feel his presence.
The path ends abruptly. It almost does not seem real.
The light is not real. How strange.
Another god. But there is something to its eye...
The Fortress. Was still there a thousand years ago, eh?
The various dragon-thrones of Old Diminor.
HEIRWATH. THE FIRST GUEST.
Today, this is a cursed land.
Oh, to hear what strange bardic nonsense these snails cooked up...
It was the drake-kin who first broke the Beasts of Jor.
Huh. Looks like some type of tourney. Fun.

What a divine view.

A shrine older than any man on the Coast.

To the beginning. Is this all just a memory?

You see him in the dark - the last son.
He is here.
You're not gonna find anything back here.

Pieces of Norvik, scatters further - here, too.
